label: Breeze
plantRateNote: Plant rate is each numbered spot's share of successful plants on that site in active-season PC Competitive.

weaponSuggestions.note: Smoke fights and close site finishes give the Phantom a narrow conversion edge, while the Vandal remains the cleaner long-lane one-tap choice.

weaponSuggestions.locations: A Main, B Main, Mid Nest
weaponSuggestions.conversion: Conversion read: the Operator wins the defense-side sniper comparison; Judge or Bucky only catches up inside a deliberately protected Tunnel or Hall pocket.
weaponSuggestions.note: On defense, the map gives repeated long-lane shots. Mobility or teleport tools make the weapon safer after contact.
Use cover and first-shot accuracy across Breeze's long pistol lanes while preserving credits for utility.

weaponSuggestions.conversion: Conversion read: the shotgun remains location-dependent and cannot match the Operator across Breeze's open sites.
weaponSuggestions.note: On defense, treat it as a protected Hall or Tunnel ambush, then recover a ranged weapon before rotating into open space.
Use it with a deliberate close-range route; most Breeze fights still expose an SMG's range limit.

defense: Mid is the strategic core of this map — mid control is less about the space itself and more about the pressure it lets you apply to both sites at once.
attack: Smoking Mid Nest removes the Operator angle that otherwise dominates that lane — a specific, repeatable utility play, not just a generic smoke.
Smoking Tunnel forces defenders into a binary choice: play the tunnel more aggressively than they'd like, or fall back and give up the space.

siteTips.label: A Pyramids
siteTips.text: Split the two pyramids into separate clears. Plant only after the close side and Back Site lane have been accounted for.

siteTips.label: A Bridge
siteTips.text: Keep Bridge denied during the plant; its elevation watches both the site crossing and several pyramid plants.

siteTips.label: B Pillar
siteTips.text: Use Pillar to isolate the first defender, then clear Back Site before spreading into the open plant lanes.

siteTips.label: B Tunnel
siteTips.text: Tunnel control shortens the defender rotation and protects a B split, but only if the Mid player can be traded.

teamplayTips.label: Mid leverage
teamplayTips.text: Keep one player connected to Mid while the site group pressures Main; that threat prevents both defenders from leaning into one entrance.

teamplayTips.label: Long trades
teamplayTips.text: Breeze spacing stretches trade distance. Say who follows the first contact before crossing an open lane.

teamplayTips.label: Late information
teamplayTips.text: Save one scan, camera, or flank trap for the rotation because a wrong site read costs more time here than on compact maps.

Duelist.text: Use movement to cross the long exposed lanes after recon or a flash removes the first angle.
Create pressure from Mid or Hall so defenders cannot hold one site entrance with every rifle.
Operator rounds need a planned escape route; do not repeat the same long angle after revealing the weapon.

Initiator.text: Scan or drone the long sightline the duelist is about to cross, not the site after contact begins.
Use Mid Nest, Tunnel, Back Site, and Hall as named utility targets so the team knows what is actually cleared.
Save one information tool for the late rotation because the distance between sites makes false reads expensive.

Controller.text: Viper-style walls are strongest when they split a site into a playable front half and an isolated defender half.
Remove Mid Nest or Tunnel when taking center control; both positions can hold multiple rotation paths.
Prioritize complete lane denial and fuel timing over difficult one-way setups on Breeze's open geometry.

Sentinel.text: Use flank utility to protect the long rotations, then survive so that information remains useful.
Anchor from off-angles that force attackers to clear after crossing open ground.
Do not stack every piece of utility on one site when Mid pressure can break the setup from behind.

compSample.note: High-rank Competitive selection reference. Map and global pick shares use the same rank window; each role layout is an observed five-agent structure.

agentInsights.Chamber: Trademark protects the long flank while Rendezvous supports aggressive Operator holds; B has the stronger current defensive success in this sample.
agentInsights.Clove: Long-range smoke placement stays useful through Breeze rotations, and post-death utility protects late hits.
agentInsights.Jett: Dash and Updraft create a safe exit from the long Operator lanes that define first contact.
agentInsights.Neon: High Gear closes Breeze's long gaps quickly enough to punish defenders before cross-map help arrives.
agentInsights.Reyna: Dismiss gives a self-sufficient escape after winning one of Breeze's exposed long-range duels.
agentInsights.Iso: Double Tap and Contingency help isolate one long sightline instead of fighting the full open site.
agentInsights.KAY/O: ZERO/point and suppression give the second-initiator layout a direct way to disable defensive utility before crossing Breeze's long lanes.
agentInsights.Sova: Recon and Drone clear wide sightlines where close-range flashes cannot cover every defender.
agentInsights.Sage: Barrier and Slow Orbs compress open entrances; A is the stronger current anchor site for her stall package.
agentInsights.Viper: Toxic Screen divides the open sites into playable halves and preserves fuel for post-plant denial.
